newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Logica's Irish buy to boost profit.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Logica's Irish buy to boost profit.

text.p: British software company Logica Plc said on Thursday its acquisition of an Irish telecoms services firm would boost its profits and revenues and dramatically increase its client base.
Logica said the acquisition of Aldiscon Ltd for up to 51.0 million stg would push its own 1997/98 profits past the 34 million stg that most analysts were predicting prior to the deal.
"We should certainly beat the analysts' estimates because we're adding a new business," chief executive Martin Read told Reuters in an interview.
"In the first full year this will be earnings enhancing," he added.
Logica forecast its pretax profits for the year to end-June at 28.1 million stg, up 14 percent compared to the previous year.
Read said the acquisition would raise Logica's telecoms sector revenues to 18 percent of total turnover from 11 percent and expand the company's services in the fast-growing mobile phone market.
Logica's shares surged seven percent, rising 47.5p to 737.5 by 0935 GMT to rank among the top percentage gainers on the London Stock Exchange.
Aldiscon specialises in short message service centres, which let users retrieve messages via mobile phones and pagers.
"They're the platform for a whole range of value-added services that are coming down the stream -- the ability to send faxes and e-mails this way and general information," Read said.
These message centres mark new territory for Logica, which currently sells mobile 'phone billing and fraud detection systems.
"It fits very closely with what we already do," Read said, noting that Aldiscon's services to clients had been limited because of its inability to link short message centres to other systems.

"(But) that is exactly the work that Logica does. So the synergistic benefit of (using) Logica's consultancy systems integration skills to match the products that Aldiscon's got have given us a very good leverage factor," he said.
The deal will also add to Logica's list of clients. Of Aldiscon's 80 global customers -- which include giants like AT&T Wireless and MCI Communications Corp -- only 15 are Logica clients.
Aldiscon had pretax profits of 3.5 million punts on turnover of 30.1 million for the year to March 31.
To fund the acquisition, Logica planned to raise 52.5 million stg net through a one-for-seven rights issue at 605p per ordinary share.
Read said the company would continue to look at buying other firms.
"Acquisition is very much part of our strategy, either building in particular market sectors or strengthening our geographical coverage," he said.
